_doc: Workflow STEP-guard registry. [OPUS-5] sparq-org/sparq#5371. The repo gates hard at the JOB level (`ci-summary / gate` + .github/advisory-registry.json) and hard INSIDE python modules (mutation-checked unit tests); the seam between them — an individual workflow STEP — was uncovered. Deleting a pre-write self-test step, or adding `continue-on-error: true` to it, left the job green, the gate green and every python test passing. scripts/check-workflow-step-guards.py reads this file and enforces three rules: S1 pins each declared safety step (it exists, is unconditional, is not swallowed, still invokes the commands that make it a guard, and still runs BEFORE the step it protects); S2 refuses any step-level `continue-on-error` inside a job that GATES unless it is waived here with a reason; S3 refuses a NEW self-test-before-write lane that is not pinned in `pinned_steps`, so this registry cannot silently go stale as workflows are added. LIMIT, stated honestly: S2 covers the declarative `continue-on-error` key only. A `run:` body that swallows its own failure with `|| true` or `set +e` is NOT detected — that idiom is used legitimately across the tree and banning it is a separate, larger piece of work.

pinned_steps.step_name: Self-test the classifier before it writes
pinned_steps.why: The half-hourly `--apply` sweep writes `area:` labels to LIVE issues, and a wrong area routes a worker at the wrong crate. These two hermetic suites are the only thing standing between a rule-table regression and mislabelled live issues. Delete the step, or let it continue-on-error, and the sweep applies unverified labels with nothing red anywhere.

pinned_steps.expected_job_if: github.event_name == 'schedule' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || (github.event_name == 'issue_comment' && github.event.issue.pull_request != null && contains(github.event.comment.body, 'VERDICT')) || (github.event_name == 'pull_request_review' && github.event.pull_request.number != null) || (github.event_name == 'workflow_run' && github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' && github.event.workflow_run.pull_requests[0].number != null)
pinned_steps.why: The bridge translates review comments into `review:` labels that the arm path keys off, using an App token with write scope. Its policy self-test (plus its transient-retry dependency's) is the pre-write guard; without it a policy regression relabels PRs and can arm on a verdict that was never given.

swallow_waivers.reason: Deliberate and documented in ci.yml: `cargo fmt --all --check` stays non-blocking until the deferred workspace-wide reformat lands (see rustfmt.toml). The step's own status stays visible in the run.

The artifact is an ATTACHMENT to the auto-filed finding, not the finding. A run that failed before the upload has no artifact; the filer renders the absence as "(no log captured …)" and the issue is still worth filing. Swallowing this download is what keeps a missing attachment from suppressing the report.

swallow_waivers.step_name: Derive the feature-OFF declaration (advisory — leg 2's result is unchanged)
swallow_waivers.reason: Advisory by construction: it only PRINTS a declaration for a human to commit and cannot make leg 2 pass. Refusal (exit 2) is its normal outcome on an unprovable diff, and swallowing it keeps that refusal from adding a second red to a job leg 2 has already failed.
